title: Rationalize audit + metadata storage to reduce join amplification and improve control-plane read latency
creator: Ava Singh
description:
Summary: The control plane currently pays a high read penalty for common queries because audit_log and resource_metadata are organized in ways that cause wide joins and repeated JSON parsing. This ticket aims to refactor storage layout, add targeted indexes and materialized aggregates, and provide a migration path that keeps live reads fast and write stall risk low.

Goals:
- Introduce a normalized metadata_summary table that extracts 4 high-cardinality columns (owner_id, resource_type, status, last_activity_at) from resource_metadata JSON and keep it transactionally updated.
- Replace a hot path join (resources JOIN resource_metadata) used by the billing and quota services with a single indexed read from metadata_summary.
- Add a compact audit_log partitioning scheme (by month + minor rolling) and a covering index for (resource_id, created_at DESC) to speed recent-history queries.
- Reduce JSON column scans by migrating frequently-used keys to first-class columns and deprecate application-side JSON_EXTRACT in hot queries.
- Provide online migrations with backfill jobs, read-fallback, and a rollback plan.

Non-Goals:
- Complete redesign of all metadata keys (this focuses on the 4 keys above).
- Changing retention policy for audit data (separate ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
1) 95th percentile latency for the billing service control-plane read in staging reduces by >=40% in representative workloads.
2) The new metadata_summary table is kept in sync in production for at least one week without drift; an automated checker reports 0 mismatches for sampled IDs.
3) Backfill completes within the SLA window (48 hours for full prod backfill); if not, we automatically switch to phased backfill.
4) Rollback path documented and exercised in staging (failover to legacy join path with a feature flag).
5) New indexes do not increase peak write latency by more than 15% in controlled load tests.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (design + tests, 1 week): schema DDLs, index proposals, sample queries, and benchmark harness on a snapshot of prod.
- Phase 2 (staging rollout, 2 weeks): deploy schema + replica-only materialized reads, start backfill job with throttling, verify checker.
- Phase 3 (canary prod, 1 week): enable reads from metadata_summary for 5% traffic, measure latencies and error rates, increase to 50% then 100% if stable.
- Phase 4 (cleanup, 1 week): add final foreign-key constraints where safe, drop deprecated JSON indexes and reduce storage.

Migration details and safety knobs:
- All DDLs use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and are deployed via online-safe migration tool (gh-migrate wrapper).
- Backfill job runs as a Kubernetes CronJob with concurrency limits and adaptive rate limiting tied to db_cpu and p95 write latency.
- Feature flag (ff:metadata_summary_reads) controls read path selection; fallback keeps legacy join until checker confirms no drift.
- Checker runs continuous sampling (1k random resources/hr) comparing legacy join vs summary; mismatches open PagerDuty to oncall-db.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New Grafana panel: control-plane read p50/p95/p99 per route pre/post migration.
- Backfill progress dashboard with rows processed, estimated time remaining, per-shard lag.
- Checker metric: mismatch_rate (expected 0) and stale_rows_detected.

Rollback plan:
- Toggle feature flag off to route reads back to legacy join.
- If backfill causes sustained write pressure, stop backfill CronJob and pause schema finalization; resume after remediation.
- In worst-case full rollback, restore audit index changes from pg_dump snapshot taken pre-change (documented runbook).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Backfill overwhelms primary during peak. Mitigation: run in low-traffic windows, adaptive rate limiting, shard backfill to replica first.
- Risk: Schema drift between summary and JSON. Mitigation: continuous checker + alerts + automated repair job that can re-queue rows for backfill.

Notes and links:
- Benchmark harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane-bench/tree/metadata-summary (work-in-progress)
- Staging PR with DDLs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4821
- Initial migration plan doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/docs/control-plane/metadata-summary-migration (internal)
